item.title: Ba reigns
item.description: JOHN Orobulu scored a hat-trick as Dayals Sawmillers Ba FC ended a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title with a commanding 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri at the 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, yesterday. The Men in Black produced a composed and dominant performance, controlling possession and showing their strength in both defence and attack from the opening whistle.
item.content:encoded:
JOHN Orobulu scored a hat-trick as Dayals Sawmillers Ba FC ended a seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title with a commanding 6-0 victory over Tailevu Naitasiri at the 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, yesterday.

The Men in Black produced a composed and dominant performance, controlling possession and showing their strength in both defence and attack from the opening whistle.

Orobulu opened the scoring in the 39th minute after Ba applied sustained pressure on the Tailevu Naitasiri defence.

Ba maintained their composure and went into halftime with a 1-0 lead.

They returned from the break with greater intensity and quickly extended their advantage.

A foul inside the penalty area in the 49th minute handed Ba a penalty, which Praneel Naidu calmly converted to make it 2-0.

Ba continued to dominate and Orobulu struck again to score his second goal of the match.

Vilitati Kautoga then added another goal as Ba continued to dismantle the Tailevu Naitasiri defence.

Orobulu completed his hat-trick to further underline Ba’s dominance before Shazil rounded off the scoring with the sixth goal.

The victory ended Ba’s seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title and added another major trophy to their cabinet after their Fiji FACT triumph earlier this season.

Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar praised his players for delivering when it mattered most.

“I’m happy with the boys. They knew a win today would make us win the title, so the boys delivered,” Kumar said.

The victory sparked celebrations in Ba as the Men in Black finally reclaimed the league crown after seven years.

The emphatic 6-0 victory not only ended Ba FC’s seven-year wait for the Extra Premier League title but also solidified their status as a dominant force in Fijian football.

This triumph adds to their impressive haul this year, complementing their 2026 BiC Fiji FACT Champions trophy won in Labasa earlier this season.

With such a strong finish to the year, Ba FC has set a high standard for themselves and will be a team to watch in the upcoming seasons.

item.title: ‘Stop them, to win’
item.description: Scoring points has never been Fiji’s problem. Stopping them, however, is where new Fiji Bati coach Mick Potter believes World Cup matches will be won and lost.
item.content:encoded:
Scoring points has never been Fiji’s problem.

Stopping them, however, is where new Fiji Bati coach Mick Potter believes World Cup matches will be won and lost.

The coach who guided Fiji to the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals in 2017, said building a disciplined defensive system without taking away the natural attacking instincts of the Bati would be his biggest priority ahead of this year’s tournament.

Drawn in Pool A alongside Australia, Switzerland and Ukraine, Potter said Fiji had to continue playing the exciting brand of rugby league it is known for.

“With the ball, we need to play the way Fiji play,” he said.

“We’ve got to open up the game a little bit to stress the opposition.”

But against the world’s leading nations, flair alone would not be enough.

Potter said Fiji had to match its attacking brilliance with defensive discipline and relentless effort.

“On the flip side, we need to make sure that our defence is pretty stout and diligent, disciplined and have a lot of energy,” he said.

He said controlling possession would also play a vital role.

Potter has little doubt the Bati possess the attacking weapons to trouble any defence.

“We’ve got the ability to score points,” he said.

He said the difference between winning and losing at a World Cup often came down to the smallest details.

“There’s attack and defence, but there’s so much in those little things, those little details and those effort areas that we’re looking at.”

Those areas, Potter believes, will determine whether Fiji can challenge the game’s traditional heavyweights once again.

item.title: Sponsorship boost for Maroons
item.description: KHELVIN Civil Engineering has stepped in as the major sponsor of the Lautoka Rugby Union, providing a timely boost as the 2026 domestic rugby season gathers momentum. Speaking after the sponsorship signing, Lautoka Rugby Union president Inoke Momoedonu said the partnership marked a significant milestone for the union, which had been without a major sponsor.
item.content:encoded:
KHELVIN Civil Engineering has stepped in as the major sponsor of the Lautoka Rugby Union, providing a timely boost as the 2026 domestic rugby season gathers momentum.

Speaking after the sponsorship signing, Lautoka Rugby Union president Inoke Momoedonu said the partnership marked a significant milestone for the union, which had been without a major sponsor.

Momoedonu thanked Khelvin Civil Engineering for placing its trust in the Maroons and pledged that the sponsorship funds would be managed responsibly and transparently.

“The 2026 rugby calendar has already commenced, and this support comes at the right time,” he said.

He added that the sponsorship would strengthen the union’s operations while helping to nurture and develop rugby talent across Lautoka.

“As volunteers running the union, this type of sponsorship is greatly needed. We are committed to ensuring the funds are utilised in a transparent financial manner, and we look forward to building a strong relationship with Khelvin Civil Engineering.”

Under the new partnership, the rugby side will officially compete as Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons Rugby, reflecting the company’s commitment to the growth of rugby in the Sugar City.

The sponsorship comes at a crucial stage of the season, with Khelvin Cviil Engineering Lautoka hosting traditional rivals McDonalds Nadi today in Round Two of the Skipper Cup and the Subrails Marama Cup competition at ground three in Churchill Park.

The clash is expected to attract a strong home crowd as the Maroons look to build momentum in front of their supporters.

item.title: Nadi women run riot
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi women’s team made a powerful statement in the second round of the Subrails Marama Cup Championship, thrashing Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons 89-12 at Churchill Park Ground Three in Lautoka on Saturday. Head coach Timaima Ravisa was pleased with the performance but said there was still room for improvement as the side continues its campaign.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi women’s team made a powerful statement in the second round of the Subrails Marama Cup Championship, thrashing Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons 89-12 at Churchill Park Ground Three in Lautoka on Saturday.

Head coach Timaima Ravisa was pleased with the performance but said there was still room for improvement as the side continues its campaign.

Ravisa said the team built on its defensive work from last week’s match against Kadavu, with defence remaining a major priority heading into the Lautoka clash.

“Our game today, we just picked up from our last game against Kadavu last week. Mainly focusing on our defence, it was my main priority,” Ravisa said.

She praised her players for maintaining their intensity until the final whistle and executing their attacking plans effectively.

“Our attack is just to attack the space, and I bet the girls showed that to me, especially working as a team to be able to score the tries,” she said.

Ravisa said the message to the players before the match and half-time was simple — play with purpose, showcase their talent and give their best.

Despite the comprehensive victory, she acknowledged there were areas the team needed to improve.

“There’s a lot of positive but a lot of walk-ons too in today’s game. So, from here we will build towards next week on our next game against Suva,” she said.

Ravisa also thanked God, her players, sponsors, executives, the union and the families and supporters who continued to back the team.

item.title: Walker confident Fijiana can rise
item.description: NEW Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker believes the side has the potential to challenge the world’s top teams as he begins building towards the Women’s Rugby World Cup. Walker who has only been in the coaching role for less than a week, said his first match provided an opportunity to assess the players and understand what the team needs to develop.
item.content:encoded:
NEW Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker believes the side has the potential to challenge the world’s top teams as he begins building towards the Women’s Rugby World Cup.

Walker who has only been in the coaching role for less than a week, said his first match provided an opportunity to assess the players and understand what the team needs to develop.

Despite the heavy loss to South Afreica, Walker said he would not have accepted the role if he did not believe the Fijiana could reach a higher level.

“I wouldn’t have taken the role if I didn’t have that belief,” Walker said.

He said the natural ability of the players and Fiji’s passion for rugby gave him confidence in the program.

Walker, however, stressed that improvement would take time and would require the team to strengthen its basic skills and standards.

“We’ve got a long period of time to build as a group because we’ve got a bigger goal in mind,” he said.

He said exposing young players to international rugby would also be important as the Fijiana continued to develop their depth.

Walker identified conditioning as another area requiring attention, saying the team was not yet at the level of Tier One nations.

He believes improving fitness and skills under pressure could lead to significant progress across the team.

“We’ve got a number of young girls in there, a couple of debutants today that have never been at this level,” Walker said.

“We always need to raise our expectations and standards throughout our team.”

Walker said the Fijiana were moving in the right direction and praised the strong bond within the squad.

The team will now use the lessons from the first match as it prepares for its next encounter against South Africa.

item.title: Rewa FC vows to bounce back
item.description: REWA FC vows to bounce back after a disappointing 1-4 defeat to Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their opening match of the OFC Men’s Champions League at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday. Captain Tevita Waranaivalu admitted Rewa failed to produce their best football in the opening half, conceding goals that he believed could have been prevented.
item.content:encoded:
REWA FC vows to bounce back after a disappointing 1-4 defeat to Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in their opening match of the OFC Men’s Champions League at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday.

Captain Tevita Waranaivalu admitted Rewa failed to produce their best football in the opening half, conceding goals that he believed could have been prevented.

“We really have to relook at our performance today (yesterday). We gave away too simple and easy goals in the first half that we could have stopped,” Waranaivalu said.

Despite the defeat, he praised his teammates for continuing to fight until the final whistle.

“The boys fought until the last minute and kept giving in the fight even though we were down.”

Waranaivalu said Rewa’s message at halftime was simple — return to their style of football and take their chances.

“We really slept off in the first half. We know that we are the better side, but we just have to play our game and finish our chances. That was what we were lacking today.”

Waranaivalu said Rewa’s preparations had also been challenging, with the squad having only one solid week together following the arrival of international players.

“It might need a little bit of time, but it is football. Whether we come one week or three days before the game, we still must play and win,” he noted.

Waranaivalu was encouraged by Rewa’s second-half performance, particularly the number of chances created.

“We created so many chances. Missing those chances really affected us. We should have closed the margin and maybe even won the game in the second half,” Waranivalu explained.

Key player Setareki Hughes was on the bench and played after halftime after carrying an injury from training.

Waranaivalu said his impact was immediately noticeable.

“He contributed so much to creating opportunities for his side in second half,” he said.

With two matches remaining, Waranaivalu believes Rewa can still fight their way into the semi-finals.

“We will go back, look at this game, take the positives, improve and come back strong in the next two games.”

He also thanked Rewa’s travelling supporters, including a busload of fans who made the journey from Nausori.

“Even though we couldn’t get you the win today, we believe we can bounce back in the next two games.”

Rewa FC will face Taupapa in their second pool match at the 4R Stadium, Govind Park, Ba, on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, starting at 4pm.

item.title: Bobo eyes Flying Fijians dream
item.description: At just 22, Ra Rugby fly-half Epeli Bobo is already dreaming of following in the footsteps of his father, former Flying Fijians star and Ra coach Sireli Bobo. Epeli was part of the Ra side that defeated Northland 17-10 in the Vodafone Vanua Cup final, ending a 28-year wait for the coveted title.
item.content:encoded:
At just 22, Ra Rugby fly-half Epeli Bobo is already dreaming of following in the footsteps of his father, former Flying Fijians star and Ra coach Sireli Bobo.

Epeli was part of the Ra side that defeated Northland 17-10 in the Vodafone Vanua Cup final, ending a 28-year wait for the coveted title.

The victory was made even more special as he played under his father, with his family watching proudly from the sideline.

“My memorable moment was looking at my mother running up and down on the field cheering me on and my dad standing on the sideline motivating us,” Bobo said. The Nawairuku, Ra native said his father’s guidance has played an important role in his development, both on and off the field.

“One main message my dad always reminds me is to always put God first in everything that I do,” he said.

Representing his vanua was another proud moment for the young playmaker.

“It’s an honour to represent my vanua and play under Dad.”

The road to the Vanua Cup triumph was not an easy one.

Bobo recalled that Ra started the season with only seven players and faced plenty of challenges along the way.

“Starting off the season, we started with seven players. It was not an easy journey. We struggled, but hats off to the boys for their commitment and hard work,” he said.

Their hard work eventually paid off when they overcame Northland in the final to lift the title after 28 years.

Now, Bobo has set his sights on a bigger goal, earning a place in the Flying Fijians squad, just like his father.

“My aim is to be a Flying Fijian just like my dad, and if I can get an overseas contract, that would be good.”

Bobo joined the Ra community yesterday in celebrating the historic triumph, a victory that he hopes will become the foundation of his own journey towards the international stage.

item.title: Rewa U16 girls make strong statement
item.description: REWA’S under-16 girls sent a strong message of intent with a commanding 7-0 victory over Nasinu girls in the Fiji FA U16 Girls Youth League 2026 at the Fiji Football Association Academy last Saturday. The Rewa U16 side controlled the match from the opening whistle, combining attacking pressure with disciplined play to keep Nasinu on the back foot throughout the contest.
item.content:encoded:
REWA’S under-16 girls sent a strong message of intent with a commanding 7-0 victory over Nasinu girls in the Fiji FA U16 Girls Youth League 2026 at the Fiji Football Association Academy last Saturday.

The Rewa U16 side controlled the match from the opening whistle, combining attacking pressure with disciplined play to keep Nasinu on the back foot throughout the contest.

Rewa’s persistence was rewarded on the scoreboard as they converted their opportunities and continued to press for more, while their defence held firm to complete a convincing clean sheet.

For coach Ronald Ravinesh Singh, the performance was the result of players making the most of an opportunity they had been waiting for.

“The girls were ready. They were looking for this opportunity to play, and we came for a win,” Singh said.

The coach said preparing the team has not always been straightforward, particularly with bringing the players together regularly for training.

“Especially with the girls, getting them together, it’s a bit hard. But nevertheless, the girls have been coming and the parents are supporting,” he said.

That support has been important as Rewa continues to develop a group of young players through the domestic youth competition.

The Fiji FA U16 Girls Youth League is designed to provide young female footballers with regular competitive experience and create a pathway towards higher levels of the sport, including national age-group selection.

The competition also offers an important platform for young players hoping to progress towards national age-group football, with Fiji set to compete at the 2026 OFC U-16 Women’s Championship in Honiara, Solomon Islands, from September 6 to 19. Singh said Rewa’s focus remains on improving the players while chasing a strong finish to the competition.

However, he acknowledged that determining the team’s exact position in the standings has been difficult because of several defaults during the campaign.

“We still don’t have the proper standing for the teams,” he said.

For now, Singh wants his players to concentrate on what they can control which includes training, improving their skills and building confidence with every match.

Yesterday’s seven-goal performance provides Rewa with valuable momentum as the young squad continue their campaign and look to turn their domestic experience into a foundation for the next level of women’s football.
